course.title: Plumbing Basics
course.tagline: Fix leaks, fit pipes and install taps and toilets like a working plumber.

days.title: Plumbing Tools and Safety
days.goal: Know the basic plumbing tools and the safety rules.

video.title: How to Fix a Leaky Sink

steps: Lay out a pipe wrench, adjustable wrench, pliers, tape measure and bucket.
Learn the first rule: turn the water off before you open any pipe.
Find the main stop tap (the tap that shuts off all water to the house) in your home.
Put on gloves and keep a towel and bucket close for drips.
days.task: Find your home stop tap and test that it shuts the water off.
days.challenge: Name every plumbing tool on your bench without looking.

quiz.q: What is the first thing to do before opening any pipe?
options: Turn the water off at the stop tap
quiz.explain: Turning the water off stops flooding before you open anything.

quiz.q: What is a stop tap?
options: The tap that shuts off all water to the house
quiz.explain: The stop tap controls all water coming into the house.

quiz.q: Why keep a bucket and towel close when plumbing?
options: To catch drips and spills from pipes
quiz.explain: Pipes always hold some water, so a bucket catches the spill.

days.title: How Water Flows in a Home
days.goal: Follow water from the street main to the tap and down the drain.

video.title: How to Fix a Leaky Sink

steps: Trace the cold water pipe from where it enters the house.
Find the hot water tank or heater and its pipes.
Learn that waste water flows downhill to the drain.
Draw a simple map of your home water pipes.
days.task: Draw a simple map of the water pipes in your home.
days.challenge: Explain to a friend where the water in a tap comes from.

days.title: Fix a Leaky Tap
days.goal: Stop a dripping tap by changing its washer.

video.title: How to Fix a Leaky Sink

steps: Turn off the water to the tap first.
Take the tap handle off and unscrew the top.
Lift out the old rubber washer and match it at a shop.
Fit the new washer, put the tap back and turn the water on.
days.task: Stop one dripping tap with a new washer.
days.challenge: Stop a drip using only parts you already have.

days.title: Find and Stop a Leak
days.goal: Find where a pipe leaks and stop the water fast.

video.title: How to Fix a Leaking Pipe

steps: Dry the pipe with a cloth, then watch where water appears first.
Turn off the stop tap to stop the flow.
Put a bucket under the leak and mop up.
Mark the leak spot with tape so you can find it again.
days.task: Find and mark a real or practice leak, then stop the water.
days.challenge: Stop a leak in under two minutes from the moment you spot it.

quiz.q: What is the most common cause of a leaking pipe?
options: A worn joint or cracked fitting
quiz.explain: Joints wear out or crack over time, and that is where leaks start.

quiz.q: How do you find a small leak?
options: Dry the pipe and watch where water appears first
quiz.explain: Drying the pipe shows exactly where the water comes from.

quiz.q: What should you do first when you find a leak?
options: Turn off the water and put a bucket under it
quiz.explain: Stopping the water and catching drips limits damage while you fix it.

days.title: Pipe Types: PVC, Copper and PEX
days.goal: Tell PVC, copper and PEX pipes apart and know what each is for.

video.title: How to Fix a Leaking Pipe

steps: Hold a white plastic PVC pipe, a copper pipe and a bendy PEX pipe.
Learn that PVC is for drains, copper for hot and cold water, PEX bends round corners.
Try bending PEX by hand and see how it flexes.
Note which pipes need glue, solder or push-fit joints.
days.task: Label three pipes with their name and one job each.
days.challenge: Pick the right pipe for a cold water line and explain why.

days.title: Cut and Measure Pipe
days.goal: Measure and cut pipe square and clean.

video.title: How to Fix a Leaking Pipe

steps: Measure the pipe twice and mark the cut with a pencil.
Cut PVC with a pipe cutter or fine saw in one steady motion.
Cut copper with a tube cutter, turning it a little at a time.
File the cut edge smooth and remove any burrs (rough bits).
days.task: Cut three pipes to exact lengths with clean square ends.
days.challenge: Cut a pipe to length with less than 2mm of error.

days.title: Project: Fix a Leaking Pipe Joint
days.goal: Repair a leaking pipe joint with a new glued joint.

video.title: How to Glue PVC Pipe

steps: Turn off the water and drain the pipe.
Cut out the leaking joint with a pipe cutter.
Clean and dry both pipe ends.
Glue a new joint in place, hold it still, and test for leaks.
days.task: Fix a leaking pipe joint so it stays dry for 24 hours.
days.challenge: Fix the joint with no glue drips on the outside.

quiz.q: What is PVC pipe used for?
quiz.explain: PVC is a plastic pipe used mainly for drains and cold water.

quiz.q: What is solvent weld glue?
options: A glue that melts PVC so pieces fuse into one
quiz.explain: Solvent weld softens the PVC surfaces so they bond as one piece.

quiz.q: Why hold a glued PVC joint still for 30 seconds?
options: So the joint sets in the right position
quiz.explain: Moving the joint too soon breaks the bond before it sets.

project.title: Fix a Leaking Pipe Joint
project.brief: Cut out a leaking joint and replace it with a new glued joint.

days.title: Solvent Weld PVC Joints
days.goal: Join PVC pipe with solvent weld glue the right way.

video.title: How to Glue PVC Pipe

steps: Solvent weld is a glue that melts PVC so the pieces fuse into one.
Clean both surfaces, then brush primer (a cleaner that prepares the surface) on.
Brush cement on both parts and push them together with a quarter turn.
Hold still for 30 seconds, then wipe off extra glue.
days.task: Make three solvent weld joints that hold water with no leaks.
days.challenge: Make a joint that holds after one hour of drying.

days.title: Thread Tape and Sealed Joints
days.goal: Seal threaded pipe joints with thread tape so they do not drip.

video.title: How to Glue PVC Pipe

steps: Thread tape is thin white tape that seals screw-thread joints.
Wrap the tape clockwise around the male thread, 4 to 5 turns.
Screw the joint together firmly with a wrench.
Turn the water on and check for drips.
days.task: Seal two threaded joints with tape and no drips.
days.challenge: Seal a joint first try with no leaks at all.

days.title: Make a Perfect PVC Cement Joint
days.goal: Make a PVC cement joint that never leaks.

video.title: How to Make the Perfect PVC Pipe Cement Joint with Solvent Weld

steps: Cut the pipe square and clean the ends.
Dry-fit the joint first (push it together without glue to check the fit).
Apply cement evenly, push together with a twist, and hold.
Wait the full drying time before turning the water on.
days.task: Make a PVC joint that passes a pressure test with no leaks.
days.challenge: Make five joints in a row with zero leaks.

quiz.q: What does primer do before solvent welding?
options: Cleans and prepares the PVC surface so the cement bonds
quiz.explain: Primer cleans and softens the surface so the cement can fuse the joint.

quiz.q: What happens if you skip primer?
options: The joint is weak and may leak
quiz.explain: Without primer the cement cannot bond well, so the joint can fail.

quiz.q: How long should you wait before turning water on after gluing PVC?
options: The full drying time on the cement tin
quiz.explain: The cement needs its full curing time to reach full strength.

days.title: Join Pipes with Elbows and Tees
days.goal: Use elbow and tee fittings to turn corners and branch pipes.

video.title: How to Make the Perfect PVC Pipe Cement Joint with Solvent Weld

steps: An elbow turns a pipe 90 degrees; a tee branches one pipe into two.
Dry-fit the whole run before you glue anything.
Glue one joint at a time, holding each still.
Check the finished run is straight and level.
days.task: Build a pipe run with two elbows and one tee, all leak-free.
days.challenge: Build a pipe run that turns two corners and stays level.

days.title: Test Your Joints for Leaks
days.goal: Pressure-test your pipework and find any weak joint.

video.title: How to Make the Perfect PVC Pipe Cement Joint with Solvent Weld

steps: Turn the water on slowly and watch every joint.
Dry each joint with a cloth, then check again after five minutes.
Mark any joint that weeps (lets out tiny drops) and redo it.
Write down which joints passed and which failed.
days.task: Test a full pipe run and record every joint as pass or fail.
days.challenge: Find a slow weep that only shows after ten minutes.

days.title: Common Solvent Weld Mistakes
days.goal: Spot the mistakes that make PVC joints leak.

video.title: Solvent Welding Mistakes to Avoid

steps: Learn the big mistakes: no primer, too little glue, moving the joint too soon.
Look at photos of bad joints and name the mistake in each.
Practise the right way: clean, prime, glue, twist, hold.
Make one joint the wrong way on scrap to see it fail.
days.task: List five solvent weld mistakes and how to avoid each.
days.challenge: Spot the mistake in a leaking joint from a photo.

quiz.q: What is the biggest solvent weld mistake?
options: Moving the joint before it sets
quiz.explain: Moving a fresh joint breaks the bond and causes a leak.

quiz.q: Why dry-fit pipes before gluing?
options: To check the fit and lengths before glue makes it permanent
quiz.explain: Dry-fitting catches wrong lengths before glue locks everything in place.

quiz.q: What should you do with a joint that weeps?
options: Cut it out and redo it
quiz.explain: A weeping joint will not heal; it must be cut out and remade.

video.title: Solvent Welding Mistakes to Avoid

steps: Cut four pipes and four elbows to size.
Dry-fit the square, then glue one joint at a time.
Check the frame is square by measuring both diagonals.
Test it under water pressure with no leaks.
days.task: Finish a square pipe frame with four leak-free joints.
days.challenge: Build the frame with all four corners exactly square.

days.title: Remove an Old Faucet
days.goal: Take out an old bathroom faucet without breaking anything.

video.title: How to Remove and Install a Bathroom Faucet

steps: Turn off the water under the sink.
Disconnect the water pipes from the faucet.
Unscrew the nuts holding the faucet to the sink.
Lift the old faucet out and clean the sink surface.
days.task: Remove an old faucet cleanly with no damage to the sink.
days.challenge: Remove a stuck faucet nut without breaking the pipe.

quiz.q: How do you remove an old faucet?
options: Turn off the water, disconnect the pipes, unscrew the nuts
quiz.explain: Water off, pipes off, nuts off, then lift the faucet out.

quiz.q: Why connect hot to the left and cold to the right?
options: It is the standard so everyone knows which is which
quiz.explain: Standard sides stop anyone scalding themselves by mistake.

quiz.q: What is a tap washer?
options: A small rubber ring that seals the tap shut
quiz.explain: The washer presses against the seat to stop water when the tap is closed.

days.title: Install a New Faucet
days.goal: Fit a new bathroom faucet so it works and does not leak.

video.title: How to Remove and Install a Bathroom Faucet

steps: Put the new faucet through the sink holes.
Tighten the nuts underneath, but not so tight they crack the sink.
Connect the hot and cold pipes to the right sides.
Turn the water on slowly and check every joint.
days.task: Install a new faucet with no leaks at the base or pipes.
days.challenge: Install a faucet that runs hot on the left, cold on the right.

days.goal: Understand the trap (the U-bend under a sink) and clear a slow drain.

video.title: How to Remove and Install a Bathroom Faucet

steps: The trap is the U-shaped pipe that holds water to block smells.
Put a bucket under the trap and unscrew it by hand.
Clean out the gunk inside and put it back.
Run water and check it drains fast with no leaks.
days.task: Clean a sink trap so the sink drains fast again.
days.challenge: Clear a slow drain without using chemicals.

days.title: How a Toilet Works
days.goal: Know every part inside a toilet tank and what it does.

video.title: FIX a Weak Flushing TOILET

steps: Lift the tank lid and name the fill valve, flapper and overflow tube.
The fill valve refills the tank; the flapper lets water into the bowl.
Watch a flush and see each part move.
Draw and label the inside of a toilet tank.
days.task: Draw and label all the parts inside a toilet tank.
days.challenge: Explain a flush to a friend using your drawing.

quiz.q: What does the flapper do in a toilet?
options: Seals the tank outlet and lifts to let water into the bowl
quiz.explain: The flapper is the rubber seal that holds tank water back until you flush.

quiz.q: Why clean the rim holes under the bowl edge?
options: Blocked holes make a weak flush
quiz.explain: Rim holes wash water around the bowl; if they are blocked, the flush is weak.

quiz.q: Where should the tank water level sit?
quiz.explain: The right level gives a full strong flush without wasting water.

days.title: Fix a Weak Flush
days.goal: Fix a toilet that flushes weakly.

video.title: FIX a Weak Flushing TOILET

steps: Check the tank water level: it should sit about 2cm below the overflow tube.
Clean the rim holes under the bowl edge with a brush.
Check the flapper seals flat and is not worn.
Adjust the chain so it has only a little slack.
days.task: Fix a weak flush so the bowl clears in one flush.
days.challenge: Fix a weak flush using only cleaning and adjustment.

steps: Check the water level, flapper, chain and rim holes.
Clean or replace the worn part you found.
Adjust the water level and chain slack.
Test with three flushes and record the result.

days.title: Toilet Chains and Flappers
days.goal: Set the chain and flapper so the flush works every time.

video.title: How to Fix a Toilet That Won't Flush

steps: The chain links the flush handle to the flapper.
Set the chain with about 1cm of slack: too loose and it will not lift.
Check the flapper sits flat and seals the hole.
Replace a flapper that is warped or stiff.
days.task: Set a chain and flapper so the toilet flushes first time, every time.
days.challenge: Fix a toilet that needs two pushes to flush.

quiz.q: What does the chain do in a toilet?
options: Links the flush handle to the flapper
quiz.explain: Pulling the handle lifts the chain, which lifts the flapper to flush.

quiz.q: How much slack should the chain have?
quiz.explain: A little slack lets the flapper seal; too much slack means it will not lift.

quiz.q: What is a flange plunger?
options: A plunger with a rubber flap that seals a toilet drain
quiz.explain: The flap fits the toilet outlet to make a tight seal for plunging.

days.title: Unblock a Toilet Safely
days.goal: Clear a blocked toilet with a plunger and an auger.

video.title: How to Fix a Toilet That Won't Flush

steps: Use a flange plunger (one with a rubber flap at the bottom) for toilets.
Push and pull hard for 15 seconds without breaking the seal.
If the plunger fails, use a toilet auger (a hand crank snake) to reach the blockage.
Flush once to test, and never flush twice if the water is rising.
days.task: Clear a blocked toilet with a plunger.
days.challenge: Clear a blockage without flooding the floor.

days.title: Replace a Flapper and Fill Valve
days.goal: Replace the two parts that cause most toilet problems.

video.title: How Do You Fix a Broken Toilet Flush

steps: Turn off the water and empty the tank.
Unhook the old flapper and clip the new one on.
Unscrew the old fill valve and fit the new one.
Turn the water on, set the level and test the flush.
days.task: Replace a flapper and fill valve so the toilet works like new.
days.challenge: Replace both parts in under 30 minutes.

quiz.q: What makes a toilet keep running?
options: A leaking flapper or a fill valve set too high
quiz.explain: If the flapper leaks or the level is too high, water keeps flowing.

quiz.q: How do you stop a running toilet?
options: Fix the flapper seal or lower the fill level
quiz.explain: Fixing the seal or the level stops the constant flow.

quiz.q: What is a fill valve?
options: The valve that refills the tank after a flush
quiz.explain: The fill valve lets water back into the tank and stops it at the right level.

video.title: How Do You Fix a Broken Toilet Flush

steps: A running toilet usually means the flapper leaks or the fill valve is set too high.
Check the flapper seal first, then the water level.
Replace the worn part you find.

steps: Check the trap first: most slow drains are blocked there.

capstone.title: Fix Three Real Plumbing Problems
capstone.brief: Fix three real plumbing problems in one home — a leak, a tap and a toilet — test them all and present the job sheet.
checks: Leak fixed and dry for 24 hours
Tap fitted or repaired with no drips
Toilet flushing strongly and silently after filling
All joints tested under water pressure
Work area left clean and tidy
Homeowner shown each fix and how it works
Job sheet shows parts, time and price
deliverables: Job sheet with parts, time and price
Photos of each fix: before and after
List of parts used with prices
Short care note for the homeowner
